lessonBlocks.title: See and try it slowly
content: Set up the instrument comfortably, tune if needed, and check that the exercise is pain-free.
Listen to a short phrase several times without touching the guitar.
Hum the rhythm and contour; note whether it rises, falls or repeats.
Find the first note, then work through the phrase one small interval at a time and compare your attempt with the reference.
Work on this week's target: Create or perform an original 4- to 8-bar example demonstrating ensemble preparation.. Begin below the suggested reference tempo of 60 BPM if accuracy is not yet secure.
Apply the skill in a musical phrase or progression; keep the pulse going through a small error.
Finish by recalling the key idea without looking and recording one observation.

lessonBlocks.title: Make music with it
lessonBlocks.content: Apply the skill to Create or perform an original 4- to 8-bar example demonstrating ensemble preparation.. Preserve the pulse and give the phrase a clear beginning and ending.

lessonBlocks.title: Recall without looking
content: What are the steps in your listen-sing-find-verify loop?
Which part of the phrase was hardest to hear accurately?

exercises.title: Listen, name and prepare
instructions: Say what you are trying to make sound or demonstrate.
Listen to a reference or hum the target before playing.
Choose a comfortable starting tempo and one observable quality target.
exercises.successCriterion: You can state the target and identify what a successful attempt should sound or feel like.

exercises.title: Focused skill drill
instructions: Use a short original phrase of three to eight notes. Sing it, clap its rhythm, locate it on one string, then play it back without the reference.
Work in short sets; pause to identify and correct one specific issue before repeating.
Only increase tempo after clean, relaxed repetitions; reduce it if accuracy or comfort declines.
exercises.successCriterion: The learner reproduces the contour and rhythm, locates the intended notes with a deliberate checking process, and can explain what was uncertain.

exercises.title: Musical application
instructions: Apply the week's exercise: Create or perform an original 4- to 8-bar example demonstrating ensemble preparation..
Play a short phrase, loop or section with a count-in and intentional ending.
Where possible, combine the new skill with one familiar skill while preserving the pulse.
exercises.successCriterion: You can complete the application with the main checkpoint in view: Demonstrate ensemble preparation in a short musical example, explain the main musical choice and identify one improvement for the next attempt.

exercises.title: Recall and reflect
instructions: Put the diagram or notes away and answer the retrieval prompts.
Record one thing that improved and one issue that still needs attention.
Choose whether the next session should repeat, simplify, mix or extend the task.
exercises.successCriterion: A clear next target is recorded and the concept can be recalled without immediately viewing the explanation.
